records.justification: The provided page text details the application process, including eligibility quizzes, application guidelines, and how to use the online grants portal, but it does not contain any information regarding grant amounts, purposes, or deadlines.

claims.text: Grants are available for amounts under £100,000.
Grants can be used for operating/core costs.
Grants can be used for capital projects.
Grants can be used for projects or specific activities.
Applications are open all year round.
There are no deadlines for applications.
Operating/core cost grants are typically 10-20% of an organisation's total annual budget.
Capital and project grants are typically 10-20% of costs.
Local community capital projects are capped at £30,000.

records.justification: The agent's text claims that grants of £100,000 and over are considered and that Trustees meet eight times per year, neither of which is supported by the page text. All other claims are directly supported or clearly implied by the provided page text.

claims.text: Grants of £100,000 and over are considered by Trustees.
Trustees meet eight times per year.
Applicants submit an Expression of Interest all year round.
There are no deadlines for submitting an Expression of Interest.
Expressions of Interest are reviewed on a rolling basis.
If an Expression of Interest is taken forward, applicants are invited to submit a full proposal.
Full proposals are considered at a board meeting.
Major grants require a total cost of at least £1 million.
For core costs, an organisation's annual income must be £1 million or over to be eligible for a major grant.
For capital or project costs, an organisation's income does not need to be over £1 million, but the total project cost must be at least £1 million.
Local community capital projects (e.g., church or village hall) are advised to apply for a regular grant via an online portal.
Grants for local community capital projects are typically up to a maximum of £30,000.
To express interest in a major grant, applicants must first check their organisation's eligibility using a quiz.
After confirming eligibility, applicants must read guidelines and use the Grants Management Portal to submit an Expression of Interest.
The Expression of Interest form asks about the organisation, its fundraising purpose, costs, shortfall, and timings.
Upon submission of the Expression of Interest, applicants receive an email confirmation and bespoke guidance within 10 working days.
If an application is potentially suitable for a major grant, the applicant will be contacted to arrange a call.
